attempts.summary: Deployed a fresh 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (node1/node2/node3, CentOS Stream 10) since none existed previously: installed mariadb-server/mariadb-server-galera/galera, configured wsrep, opened firewalld galera+mysql services, generated an SST auth password and app credentials directly on node1 (transferred to node2/node3 over the cluster SSH keypair, never printed to the transcript), and worked around an SELinux mysqld_t self-connectto AVC denial (a known gap in the EL10 policy for mariabackup SST) by compiling and loading a minimal custom policy module on all three nodes rather than disabling enforcement. Bootstrapped node1, joined node2 and node3 via mariabackup SST, verified 3/3 Synced. Created appdb.orders with an initial committed row, then executed the required maintenance-window drill: inserted a second committed row, took a full baseline, stopped mariadb on node2, node3, then node1 last (preserving safe_to_bootstrap on node1), confirmed the cluster fully down, then bootstrapped node1 and rejoined node2/node3 — both rows present on all three nodes with cluster_size=3/Synced. Finally ran the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured each node's boot_id and healthy service/data state, rebooted node2, node3, and node1 one at a time (never overlapping), polled until each came back, proved boot_id changed each time, and verified mariadb auto-started, rejoined with full quorum (cluster_size=3, Synced), and both data rows intact after each restart.
